Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The umpires are on the field and the Namibia Under-19 run out to take their respective positions on the field. Sam Konstas and Harry Dixon are the opening batters for Australia Under-19. Jack Brassell has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, that is it from the first innings were the Australia Under-19 bowlers wreaked havoc upon the batters and troubled them throughout the innings. Namibia Under-19 failed to cross the three-digit mark and ended up at just 91 runs. The Aussie batters will be a bit relaxed going into the chase with the pressure of the required run rate out of the question but they will have to make sure not to lose many wickets at the start. Grab a cup of coffee and join us in a bit for the run chase where Australia Under-19 will chase 92 runs.

The man of the moment, Callum Vidler is in for a chat. He says that it was a great surface, similar to home. Adds that there was a bit of bounce on this surface. Mentions that Charlie Anderson bowled dots which helped him to capitalise. Shares that he likes to watch Pat Cummins bowl and tries to see what he does. Adds that his focus is on bowling quickly. Shares that they have a really good group and they are bonding well.

Australia Under-19, on the other hand, were brilliant with their planning, and the skipper, Hugh Weibgen was very sharp with their bowling changes as well. The Pacers started off well with the duo of Charlie Anderson and Callum Vidler piling up the dot balls for the first 10 overs. After that, it was more pace but a different duo consisting of Tom Straker and Mahli Beardman who wreaked havoc for the next phase of the innings. Spin was introduced pretty late in the innings by handing the ball to Rafael Macmillan who went for plenty in his first over but bounced back strongly taking the wicket of the opposition skipper. Callum Vidler was the pick of the bowlers as he scalped 4 wickets. Tom Straker clinched 3 along with a couple from Mahli Beardman. Charlie Anderson went wicketless but his disciplined bowling allowed Callum Vidler to strike early on in the innings. They will be happy with their combined bowling effort and the batters will be a bit relaxed for the second innings.

Namibia Under-19 were put under pressure from the first delivery by the opposition pacers. They didn’t try to attack them and just kept knocking the ball around, not scoring many runs. Johannes De Villiers was the first batter to fall prey to the bowlers followed by Johannes Visagie. After that, Gerhard Van Rensburg and Zacheo Vuuren managed to play out a few overs and looked to settle in when Gerhard Van Rensburg was dismissed. Zacheo Vuuren had found the fence a few times and looked to be batting with patience but he also had to walk back to the pavilion. Ryan Moffett, Jack Brassell, Henry Van Wyk, and Peter-Daniel Blignaut all were dismissed in quick succession before they could do much damage. Alexander Volschenk, the skipper, was playing a strong knock and taking on the bad balls but he too crumbled under pressure followed by Junior Kariata, the last batter to be dismissed. Only three batters managed to put up double-digit scores for Namibia Under-19 and they ended their innings with a very low total of 91 runs.

Australia Under-19 will be the happier of the two sides walking back in for the innings break. Namibia Under-19 were struggling from the start and failed to build strong partnerships. They were blown away by the bowlers and managed to put just 91 runs on the board. Callum Vidler walks back with his best bowling figures of  [8.1-3-17-4]

OUT! CASTLED! Callum Vidler rattles the woodwork again and brings an end to Namibia's struggles with the bat! Vidler continues from over the wicket and hurls a searing yorker, right at the base of the middle stump, Junior Kariata backs away and tries to give himself room. He fails to get his bat down in time as he gets beaten for pace. The ball sneaks under his bat and goes on to uproot the middle stump. Callum Vidler finishes with four wickets and Namibia Under-19 have been bowled out for just 91!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the national anthems and the two umpires have made their way out to the middle. Hugh Weibgen with some last words in the Australian huddle before they disperse to take their respective field positions. They are joined by the two Nambiian openers who stride out to the centre. It will be Gerhard Van Rensburg and Johannes De Villiers to open the innings for Namibia Under-19. Charlie Anderson will start the proceedings with the new ball for Australia Under-19. Off we go...

We are nearing the start of this game, but before that, Hugh Weibgen and Alexander Volschenk will lead their respective sides out along with their mascots for the national anthems. It will be Namibia's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is pitchside. He says that the dimensions are pretty equal and it is a brand new surface. Scott Styris adds that the decision to bowl first will favour Australia and that it looks like a traditional white ball pitch with very fine grass. Adds that side way movement will be a little less with spin to come in a bit late. He ends by mentioning it could be easier to bat on as we progress in the game.

The captain of Namibia Under-19, Alexander Volschenk says that they are not bothered at all but they would have looked to bowl first as well. Feels that there will be something in it for the first ten overs. Mentions that the team is ready for the tournament. Further adds that they have batted first in some practice games and bowled first in some, so they were prepared to do both. Ends by informing that they are going with 5 batters and 2 all-rounders.

The skipper of Australia Under-19, Hugh Weibgen says that they will bowl first because he thinks that they will feel comfortable chasing. Adds that they are prepared well for these conditions. Mentions that they want to follow in the steps of the senior team and start off with a win. He ends by mentioning his team of 6 batters, a keeper and 4 pace options.

Namibia Under-19 (Playing XI) - Gerhard Van Rensburg, Johannes De Villiers, Johannes Visagie (WK), Zacheo Vuuren, Alexander Volschenk (C), Ryan Moffett, Jack Brassell, Henry Van Wyk, Peter-Daniel Blignaut, Hanro Badenhorst, Junior Kariata.

Australia Under-19 (Playing XI) - Harry Dixon, Sam Konstas, Hugh Weibgen (C), Harjas Singh, Ryan Hicks (WK), Corey Wasley, Rafael Macmillan, Charlie Anderson, Tom Straker, Mahli Beardman, Callum Vidler.
TOSS - Australia Under-19 have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

Namibia Under-19, on the other hand, will have to adapt to these conditions because their warm-up games were abandoned. Johannes De Villiers, Alexander Volschenk, Gerhard Van Rensburg, and Johannes Visagie will be the pillars of the batting lineup while Jack Brassell, Zacheo Vuuren, and Peter-Daniel Blignaut will be expected to provide wickets at crucial times They will want to defeat the Aussies and cause a massive upset right at the start of the tournament. Stay tuned as we bring you the toss and team news shortly.

The Aussies have faced a loss against Bangladesh U-19 in the warm-up game. With a hope to start off strongly, they will give it their all in this encounter. The skipper, Hugh Weibgen is expected to contribute heavily with the bat along with Harjas Singh, and Corey Wasley. Charlie Anderson and Callum Vidler will spearhead the bowling unit with equal support from others. They will want to start off their campaign with a win and boost their morale.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. We are at the Diamond Oval in Kimberly and it is time for match number 9 of the ICC U19 World Cup. This match will be played between Australia Under-19 and Namibia Under-19 and it is expected to provide a lot of entertainment for the viewers.
